title: 低端机卡顿根因：kswapd、direct reclaim、compaction 与 UI 抖动
key_conclusions: Low-memory jank is strongest when frame misses align with PSI memory stalls and direct reclaim or compaction counters.
kswapd activity alone is not enough to prove jank; the stronger signal is caller-visible stall on UI, RenderThread, Binder, or hot worker threads.
Direct reclaim and compaction require different fixes: allocation-rate reduction for reclaim, contiguous-allocation reduction for compaction.
Perfetto, vmstat, PSI, zoneinfo, pagetypeinfo, and gfx frame data must be collected as one timeline.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real Perfetto trace with frame misses aligned to direct reclaim.
It does not include device-specific vmstat counter names across Android kernel versions.
It does not quantify jank thresholds for PSI some/full or allocstall deltas.
It does not include runnable low-RAM reproduction workloads.
discovered_connections: Day 50's low/min watermark breach explains why Day 51's allocation stalls happen in foreground code paths.
Day 49's reclaim counters become actionable only after they are aligned with frame misses and PSI.
Graphics and large image allocations from Days 45 and 46 can trigger compaction, not only ordinary reclaim.
A background cache or prefetch optimization can still harm foreground smoothness by pushing the system below watermarks.

knowledge_gaps: Need real low-end device traces showing kswapd, direct reclaim, compaction, PSI, and FrameTimeline together.
Need practical thresholds for PSI and allocstall that distinguish noise from user-visible jank.

Need before/after examples proving cache, image, or buffer fixes reduce both stalls and frame misses.
